title: Harary's edge reconstruction conjecture
statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$) be a finite simple graph with $|E|>4$. For each edge of $G$, let $G_i$ denote the maximal subgraph obtained by deleting that edge, and define the **edge deck** of $G$ by

$$
\operatorname{Deck}(G)\coloneqq\{G_i\}_{i=1}^m.
$$

**Harary's reconstruction conjecture.** If $\operatorname{Deck}(G)=\operatorname{Deck}(H)$ for some graph $H$, then $G\cong H$.

This conjecture asserts that every graph with more than four edges is uniquely determined, up to isomorphism, by its maximal edge-deleted subgraphs. The paper proves it for graphs with exactly one cycle and three non-isomorphic subtrees; the general conjecture remains open.
source_name: Anthony E. Pizzimenti and Umarkhon Rakhimov, “Reconstructing edge-deleted unicyclic graphs”, arXiv:2411.03133 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.03133

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).
